correctness.rationale: The self-contained proof uses the exact Kraft identity to identify the critical exponent, a full b-ary de Bruijn digit cycle with primitive digit period b^k, and a deterministic complete-prefix-code parser on b^k residues. Any parser cycle has length n between b^k/L and b^k; primitivity follows because a smaller original-symbol period forces premature return of a residue. Different symbol shifts start at different de Bruijn positions, hence their common coded digit prefix has length at most k-1; strong separation multiplies the symbolic scale by at least delta. These give n*eta^s >= (b/L)delta^s at all large orders. Direct symbolic manipulations and representative finite checker runs (three codes) corroborate, but do not replace, the infinite combinatorial proof. Limits: strong separation and complete code are essential hypotheses.
